text:
A small bar magnet placed with its axis 
at $30^{o}$ with an external field of 0.06 T 
experiences a torque of 0.018 Nm. The 
minimum work required to rotate it from its 
stable to unstable equilibrium position is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Torque on a bar magnet :

$τ=MB\sin θ$

Here, $θ$ = 30º, I = 0.018 N-m, B = 0.06 T

$0.018=M\times 0.06\times 0.5$

$\Rightarrow M=0.6Am^{2}$

$W=U_{f}-U_{i}$

$=MB(\cos θ_{i}-\cos θ_{f})$

$=0.6\times 0.06(1-(-1))$

$=7.2\times 10^{-2}J$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
Take the breakdown voltage of the 
zener diode used in the given circuit as 6V. 
For the input voltage shown in figure below, 
the time variation of the output voltage is: 
(Graphs drawn are schematic and not to scale)

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The two Zener diodes are connected back to back across the output, so in either half-cycle one of them is forward biased and the other is reverse biased.

The pair conducts only when the reverse-biased diode breaks down, that is when $|V_{in}|>6\text{V}$ (forward drop neglected). The output is then held at $+6\text{V}$ in the positive half-cycle and at $-6\text{V}$ in the negative half-cycle, the extra input voltage dropping across $R_{1}$.

For $|V_{in}|<6\text{V}$ the pair does not conduct, no current flows through $R_{1}$ and $V_{o}=V_{in}$.

So the output follows the $\pm 10\text{V}$ input near zero and is clipped flat at both the positive and the negative peaks.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text: A beam of plane polarised light of large cross-sectional area and uniform intensity of $3.3 Wm^{-2}$ falls normally on a polariser (cross sectional area 3 $\times$ $10^{-4} m^{2})$ which rotates about its axis with an angular speed of 31.4 rad/s. The energy of light passing through the polariser per revolution, is close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The polariser rotates at $ω=31.4\text{rad s}^{-1}$, so the angle between the plane of polarisation and its pass axis is $θ=ωt$, and by Malus's law the transmitted intensity is $I=I_{0}\cos ^{2}ωt$.

Over one revolution the average of $\cos ^{2}ωt$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}$, so the average transmitted intensity is $\dfrac{I_{0}}{2}=\dfrac{3.3}{2}=1.65\text{W m}^{-2}$.

Time for one revolution: $T=\dfrac{2π}{ω}=\dfrac{2\times 3.14}{31.4}=0.2\text{s}$.

Energy passing through the polariser (area $A=3\times 10^{-4}\text{m}^{2}$) per revolution:

$E=\dfrac{I_{0}}{2}AT=1.65\times (3\times 10^{-4})\times 0.2=9.9\times 10^{-5}\text{J}\approx 1.0\times 10^{-4}\text{J}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text: For a transverse wave travelling along a straight line, the distance between two peaks (crests) is 5 m, while the distance between one crest and one trough is 1.5 m. The possible wavelengths (in m) of the wave are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Any two crests are a whole number of wavelengths apart, and a crest and a trough are an odd number of half wavelengths apart:

$5=nλ,1.5=(2m+1)\dfrac{λ}{2}\Rightarrow 3=(2m+1)λ$

Here $n=1,2,3,\ldots$ and $m=0,1,2,\ldots$. Dividing the two relations:

$\dfrac{n}{2m+1}=\dfrac{5}{3}\Rightarrow 3n=5(2m+1)$

So $2m+1$ must be a multiple of 3, and since it is odd, $2m+1=3p$ with $p=1,3,5,\ldots$ Then

$λ=\dfrac{3}{2m+1}=\dfrac{1}{p}=1,\dfrac{1}{3},\dfrac{1}{5},\ldots \text{m}$

For example, $λ=\dfrac{1}{3}\text{m}$ puts 15 wavelengths between the two crests and 4.5 wavelengths between the crest and the trough.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text: Particle A of mass $m_{A} =$ $\frac{m}{2}$ moving along the x-axis with velocity $v_{0}$ collides elastically with another particle B at rest having mass $m_{B} =$ $\frac{m}{3}$. If both particles move along the x-axis after the collision, the change $\Deltaλ$ in de-Broglie wavlength of particle A, in terms of its de-Broglie wavelength ($λ_{0}$) before collision is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Applying momentum conservation

$\frac{m}{2}\times V_{0}+\frac{m}{3}\times 0=\frac{m}{2}V_{A}+\frac{m}{3}V_{B}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{V_{0}}{2}=\frac{V_{A}}{2}+\frac{V_{B}}{3}$ .....(1)

Since, collision is elastic (e = 1)

e = 1 = $\frac{V_{B}-V_{A}}{V_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{0} = V_{B} – V_{A} .....(2)$

On solving (1) & (2) :

$V_{A} =$ $\frac{V_{0}}{5}$

Now, De-Broglie wavelength of A before collision :

$λ_{0}$ = $\frac{h}{m_{A}V_{0}}$

= $\frac{h}{\left (\frac{m}{2}\right )V_{0}}$

= $\frac{2h}{mV_{0}}$

Final De-Broglie wavelength :

$λ_{f}$ = $\frac{h}{m_{A}V_{A}}$

= $\frac{h}{\left (\frac{m}{2}\right )\left (\frac{V0}{5}\right )}$ = $\frac{10h}{mV_{0}}$

Now, $\Deltaλ$ = $λ_{f}$ - $λ_{0}$

= $\frac{10h}{mV_{0}}$ - $\frac{2h}{mV_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Deltaλ$ = $\frac{8h}{mV_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Deltaλ$ = $4\times \frac{2h}{mV_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Deltaλ$ = 4$λ_{0}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
Blocks of masses m, 2m, 4m and 8m are arranged in a line on a frictionless floor. Another block of
mass m, moving with speed v along the same line (see figure) collides with mass m in perfectly
inelastic manner. All the subsequent collisions are also perfectly inelastic. By the time the last block
of mass 8m starts moving the total energy loss is p% of the original energy. Value of 'p' is close to :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
All collisions are perfectly inelastic, so after the final collision, all blocks are moving together. So let the
final velocity be v', so on applying momentum conservation :

mv = 16mv'

$\Rightarrow$ v' = $\frac{v}{16}$

Now initial energy $E_{i} =$ $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

Final energy : $E_{f} =$ $\frac{1}{2}\times 16m\left (\frac{v}{16}\right )^{2}$

Energy loss : $E_{i} – E_{f}$

= $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$ - $\frac{1}{2}\times m\left (\frac{v}{16}\right )^{2}$

= $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\left [1-\frac{1}{16}\right ]$

= $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\left [\frac{15}{16}\right ]$

Total energy loss is p% = 
     Energy loss
     Original energy
 $\times$ 100

= $\frac{\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\left [\frac{15}{16}\right ]}{\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}}\times 100$

= 93.75% $\simeq$ 94 %
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

text:
In the line spectra of hydrogen atoms, difference between the largest and the shortest wavelengths of the Lyman series is 304 $A^{0}$. The corresponding difference for the Paschan series in $A^{0}$ is :
$___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For Lyman series :

Shortest wavelength, 

$λ_{s}$ = $R.1^{2}\left (\frac{1}{1^{2}}-\frac{1}{\infty ^{2}}\right )$

longest wavelength, 

$λ_{l}$ = $R.1^{2}\left (\frac{1}{1^{2}}-\frac{1}{2^{2}}\right )$

Given, $λ_{l}$ - $λ_{s}$ = 304 $A^{0}$

$\therefore$ $R.1^{2}\left (\frac{1}{1^{2}}-\frac{1}{2^{2}}\right )$ - $R.1^{2}\left (\frac{1}{1^{2}}-\frac{1}{\infty ^{2}}\right )$ = 304

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{R}$ = 912 $A^{0}$

For Paschen series :

Shortest wavelength, 

$λ_{s}$ = $R.1^{2}\left (\frac{1}{3^{2}}-\frac{1}{\infty ^{2}}\right )$ = $\frac{R}{9}$

longest wavelength, 

$λ_{l}$ = $R.1^{2}\left (\frac{1}{3^{2}}-\frac{1}{4^{2}}\right )$ = $\frac{7R}{144}$ 

$\therefore$ $λ_{l}$ - $λ_{s}$

= $\frac{144}{7R}-\frac{9}{R}$

= $\left (\frac{144}{7}-9\right )\frac{1}{R}$

= $\left (\frac{144}{7}-9\right )\times 912$ = 10553 $A^{0}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot

We know, $\Delta U = nC_{v}\Delta$T

$\Rightarrow$ $(20 + 20) = 0.15 T_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $T_{f} = 266.67$

text:
ABC is a plane lamina of the shape of an equilateral triangle. D, E are mid points of AB, AC and G is
the centroid of the lamina. Moment of inertia of the lamina about an axis passing through G and
perpendicular to the plane ABC is $I_{0}$
. If part ADE is removed, the moment of inertia of the remaining
part about the same axis is $\frac{NI_{0}}{16}$ where N is an integer. Value of N is $______$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a uniform equilateral triangular lamina of mass $m$ and side $l$, the moment of inertia about the perpendicular axis through its centroid has the form $I_{0}=kml^{2}$, with $k$ a fixed number.

Joining the midpoints D, E and F (of BC) divides the lamina into four congruent equilateral triangles, each of side $\dfrac{l}{2}$ and mass $\dfrac{m}{4}$.


[IMG]

The middle triangle DEF has the same centroid G as ABC, so about the axis through G

$I_{DEF}=k\left (\dfrac{m}{4}\right )\left (\dfrac{l}{2}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{kml^{2}}{16}=\dfrac{I_{0}}{16}$

The corner triangles ADE, BDF and CEF are carried into one another by $120^{\circ }$ rotations about G, so each has the same moment of inertia $I$ about this axis:

$3I+\dfrac{I_{0}}{16}=I_{0}\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{5I_{0}}{16}$

Removing ADE leaves

$I_{\text{remaining}}=I_{0}-\dfrac{5I_{0}}{16}=\dfrac{11\quad I_{0}}{16}\Rightarrow N=11$

Hence, the answer is 11.

text:
In a compound microscope, the magnified virtual image is formed at a distance of 25 cm from the
eye-piece. The focal length of its objective lens is 1 cm. If the magnification is 100 and the tube
length of the microscope is 20 cm, then the focal length of the eye-piece lens (in cm) is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$L = 20, f_{0} = 1cm, M = 100$

$M=\frac{v_{0}}{u_{0}}\left (1+\frac{D}{f_{e}}\right )$

$\therefore$ $M=\frac{L}{f_{0}}\left (1+\frac{D}{f_{e}}\right )$ [$v_{0}$ $\approx$ $L, u_{0}$ $\approx$ $f_{0}$]

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{20}{1}\left (1+\frac{25}{f_{e}}\right )$ = 100

on solving we get

$f_{e} = 6.25 cm$

text:
A circular disc of mass M and radius R is rotating about its axis with angular speed $ω_{1}$
. If another
stationary disc having radius $\frac{R}{2}$ and same mass M is dropped co-axially on to the rotating disc.
Gradually both discs attain constant angular speed $ω_{2}$
 the energy lost in the process is p% of the
initial energy. Value of p is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I_{f}ω_{f}=I_{i}ω_{i}$

$I_{i}=\frac{MR^{2}}{2}$

$I_{f}=\frac{MR^{2}}{2}+\frac{M(R/2)^{2}}{2}$

$=\frac{5}{4}.\frac{MR^{2}}{2}$

$\left [\frac{MR^{2}}{2}+\frac{M}{2}\left (\frac{R}{2}\right )^{2}\right ]ω^{'}=\left (\frac{MR^{2}}{2}\right ).ω$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left [\frac{MR^{2}}{2}.\left (\frac{5}{4}\right )\right ]ω^{'}=\frac{MR^{2}}{2}ω$

$ω^{'}=\frac{4}{5}ω$

loss of K.E. = $\frac{Loss}{K_{i}}\times 100$

= $\frac{\frac{1}{2}Iω^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{5}{4}I\right )\left (\frac{4}{5}ω\right )^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}Iω^{2}}$ $\times$ 100

= $\frac{ω^{2}-\frac{16}{25}ω^{2}\left (\frac{5}{4}\right )}{ω^{2}}$ $\times$ 100 = $\left (1-\frac{80}{100}\right )\times 100$

= 20%
